svg.font-family: system-ui, -apple-system, 'Segoe UI', Roboto, Helvetica, Arial, sans-serif
svg.title: Two judgments, one gate
svg.desc: One document goes to two judges. Jev, TypeSafe's System One model, answers typed questions: one choice among the categories with a certainty, and a separate yes or no for each category; it gives no reason and no quote, and its failure is a confident wrong choice. The reader, a language model, reads the whole text and answers yes or no for every category with a reason and word-for-word quotes that the code checks; its failure is that it always answers and can be swayed by the document's wording. A gate in code files the document only when both name the same single category, Jev's yes or no for it is at least 0.5, and Jev's certainty is at or above the threshold. Everything else goes to a person as needs review, or is set aside as could not process.
svg.text: One document
its full text and outline, plus every category definition
(the same input goes to both judges)
Judge one: Jev, a model built for judgments
WHAT IT IS
TypeSafe's System One model (pinned to jev-1.13.0). It does not write
prose. It answers typed questions with probabilities and says how sure it is.
WHAT IT IS ASKED
Which one category fits best, or none of these? (one question)
Does the document meet this category? (one yes/no question per category,
each judged on its own, including the category's "not for" exclusions)
WHAT IT ANSWERS (illustrative values)
Choice: Leases · certainty 0.96 · a share for every option
Yes/no per category: Leases 0.93 · Invoices 0.04 · Insurance policies 0.07
The certainty and the yes/no values are two separate answers; nothing adds them up.
HOW IT FAILS
A confident wrong choice on a document unlike anything the definitions describe.
It cannot show its evidence: no reason, no quote. Its numbers are trained to be
calibrated, and still have to be checked on your own documents.
Judge two: the reader, a large language model
WHAT IT IS
A language model that reads the whole text (GPT-5.4 on the owner's
site, GPT-6 Sol in the generic pack). A reply from the wrong model stops the run.
WHAT IT IS ASKED
For every category: yes or no, a short reason, and up to three quotes copied
word for word from the document. It is told not to choose a filing label and
to treat the document as evidence, never as instructions.
WHAT IT ANSWERS (illustrative values)
Leases: yes. "This lease agreement is made on the first day of…"
Invoices: no. Insurance policies: no.
Every quote must appear in the text word for word, or the reply fails.
HOW IT FAILS
It always answers, and any confidence it states is just more generated text.
It can be swayed by the document's own wording. The exact-quote check and
the second judge are the guards against that.
choice, certainty, yes/no per category
yes/no per category (the quotes are for the person)
The agreement gate: code, not a model
Agree = Jev's one choice is category T, its yes/no for T is at least 0.5,
and the reader said yes to T and to no other category.
The two judges' numbers are never averaged or multiplied together.
Filed (rule R1)
They agree, and Jev's certainty is at or above the
threshold (90% to start). The only rule that files.
Needs review (rules R2 to R5)
Agree but not sure enough · fits two categories ·
neither sees a category · they disagree (looked at first)
Could not process (rule R0)
A step failed: no text layer, an unsupported file,
a reply that fails its checks. The reason is recorded.
A person decides every document that was not filed, with both judges' answers beside it. Their folder moves come back as corrections.
